newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace empire plans shake-up after Gianni murder.
newsitem.headline: Versace empire plans shake-up after Gianni murder.

text.p: Santo Versace, who took over the helm of the Italian fashion house after the murder last month of his designer brother Gianni, has called a shareholders' meeting for mid-September to approve a corporate shake-up.
Italy's Official Gazette published the company's announcement on Tuesday.

Santo and younger sister Donatella took over running the multi-million-dollar style empire after Gianni was shot dead on the steps of his Miami Beach mansion last month. His alleged killer, Andrew Cunanan, who was also wanted for a string of other murders, later shot himself and the motive for the designer's slaying remains unclear.
The biggest planned change in the structure of the Versace group would be the incorporation into Gianni Versace SpA of three firms controlled and chaired by Santo -- Modifin, Istante Versa and Alias.

Both Santo and Donatella were in partnership with their brother before his death -- Santo as the business brains and Donatella as a talented designer in her own right. Most of the companies' stock is controlled by the Versace family.
The family had been believed to be preparing to launch the company on the Milan stock exchange by June 1998, but the plans were never officially confirmed.
No-one was available at Versace for comment on the proposed changes to the group's structure and the date of the shareholders' meeting was not known.
